title: The apostles' joy in dishonor for Jesus' name
english: For this reason the chorus of the apostles went up from the council of the Jews rejoicing—not only because of the kingdom of heaven, but because they had been counted worthy to be dishonored for the name of Jesus. This very thing, even by itself, is the greatest honor, and a crown, and a prize, and a source of unfading pleasure.

orientation: Olympiodorus is explaining why suffering for the truth is itself a prize, and now turns to the example of the apostles rejoicing after being dishonored by the Jewish council.

title: The contest of slander is great
english: This contest of slander is not small but very great. So Solomon, wanting to present the harshness of the contest, says: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1). But if the contest is great, then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still.

title: The greater crown and Christ's command to rejoice
english: Since the contest is great, it is very clear that the crown laid upon it is greater still. For this reason Christ commands those contending in this contest to rejoice and leap for joy, with the fitting endurance.
